seoTitle: How to Add SVG to Squarespace: Embed a Logo File Easily
metaDescription: Add an SVG logo or icon to your Squarespace site using a Code block — the most reliable method for scalable, resolution-independent graphics.
intro: SVG files are ideal for logos and icons because they stay sharp at any size, but Squarespace doesn't let you upload them like a standard image. This guide shows the most reliable way to embed SVG code on a Squarespace page using a Code block, plus what to check if it doesn't render.

steps.heading: Log in and open the editor
steps.body: Sign in at squarespace.com, select your site, and click Edit to reach the section of the page where you want the SVG to appear.

steps.heading: Add a Code block
steps.body: Click Add Block and choose Code, then paste your raw SVG markup directly into the code editor and click Apply.

steps.heading: Turn off Display Source
steps.body: If the SVG doesn't show up, check that "Display Source" is turned off in the Code Block settings — leaving it on shows the raw code instead of rendering the graphic.

steps.heading: Save your changes
steps.body: Once the SVG renders correctly, click Save to publish it to your live site.

faq.question: Can I just upload an SVG file like a regular image in Squarespace?
faq.answer: Not reliably — the Code block method, pasting the raw SVG markup, is the most consistent way to get an SVG to display correctly.

faq.question: Why isn't my SVG showing up after I added it?
faq.answer: This is often because "Display Source" is still enabled in the Code Block settings, which shows the code text instead of rendering the image.

faq.question: Why use SVG instead of a JPG or PNG for a logo?
faq.answer: SVGs are lightweight and scale without losing quality, making them ideal for logos, icons, and other graphics that need to look sharp at any size.

faq.question: Does this method work for animated icons too?
faq.answer: Yes, the Code block approach works for animated SVGs as well as static logos and icons.
